prompt: Name an animal native to Australia

answers.name: Kangaroo
answers.fact: A red kangaroo can cover about 8 metres in a single hop.

answers.name: Koala
answers.fact: Sleeps up to 20 hours a day, partly because gum leaves are so low in energy.

answers.name: Emu
answers.fact: Australia's army lost the 1932 'Emu War'.

answers.name: Wombat
answers.fact: Its poo comes out in cubes.

answers.name: Platypus
answers.fact: Glows blue-green under UV light, and the males have venomous ankle spurs.

answers.name: Kookaburra
answers.fact: A giant kingfisher whose call sounds like laughter.

answers.name: Echidna
answers.fact: One of only a handful of mammals that lay eggs.

answers.name: Dingo
answers.fact: Arrived in Australia at least 3,500 years ago.

answers.name: Quokka
answers.fact: Rottnest Island means 'rat nest': a Dutch explorer mistook quokkas for giant rats.

answers.name: Thylacine
answers.fact: The last known one died in Hobart's zoo in 1936.

answers.name: Sugar glider
answers.fact: Can glide about 50 metres between trees.

answers.name: Tasmanian devil
answers.fact: One of the strongest bites for its size of any mammal.

answers.name: Wallaby
answers.fact: Not a single species: there are dozens of kinds of wallaby.

answers.name: Cassowary
answers.fact: Carries a dagger-like claw on each foot.

answers.name: Possum
answers.fact: Not related to the American opossum.

answers.name: Galah
answers.fact: Also Aussie slang for a fool.

answers.name: Sulphur-crested cockatoo
answers.fact: Can live past 70. One called Cocky Bennett reportedly reached 120.

answers.name: Lyrebird
answers.fact: Can mimic chainsaws and camera shutters.

answers.name: Frill-necked lizard
answers.fact: Featured on Australia's old 2-cent coin.

answers.name: Saltwater crocodile
answers.fact: The largest living reptile on Earth.

answers.name: Freshwater crocodile
answers.fact: Shyer than the saltie, with a narrow snout built for fish.

answers.name: Goanna
answers.fact: The name comes from 'iguana', though goannas are monitor lizards.

answers.name: Blue-tongued lizard
answers.fact: Flashes that blue tongue to scare off predators.

answers.name: Bearded dragon
answers.fact: Waves one arm to signal submission.

answers.name: Redback spider
answers.fact: A close relative of the black widow.

answers.name: Funnel-web spider
answers.fact: Nobody has died from a bite since the antivenom arrived in 1981.

answers.name: Huntsman spider
answers.fact: Big, fast and startling, but not dangerous to people.

answers.name: Inland taipan
answers.fact: The most toxic venom of any land snake, but it rarely meets people.

answers.name: Eastern brown snake
answers.fact: Behind more snakebite deaths in Australia than any other snake.

answers.name: Tiger snake
answers.fact: Named for its banded stripes.

answers.name: Red-bellied black snake
answers.fact: A frog-lover, often found near water.

answers.name: Carpet python
answers.fact: Often turns up in roof cavities, hunting rats.

answers.name: Budgerigar
answers.fact: Wild budgies are always green and yellow.

answers.name: Rainbow lorikeet
answers.fact: Has a brush-tipped tongue for lapping up nectar.

answers.name: Australian magpie
answers.fact: Swooping season peaks in spring, while they guard their nests.

answers.name: Australian white ibis
answers.fact: Nicknamed the 'bin chicken' for raiding city rubbish.

answers.name: Bilby
answers.fact: Chocolate Easter bilbies are sold to raise money for the real thing.

answers.name: Wallaroo
answers.fact: Sized somewhere between a kangaroo and a wallaby.

answers.name: Quoll
answers.fact: A spotty, carnivorous marsupial being reintroduced to parts of the mainland.

answers.name: Bandicoot
answers.fact: Crash Bandicoot is meant to be an eastern barred bandicoot.

answers.name: Rosella
answers.fact: Named after Rose Hill, near Parramatta, where colonists first saw them.

answers.name: Satin bowerbird
answers.fact: Males decorate their bowers with blue things, bottle caps included.

answers.name: Black swan
answers.fact: Europeans assumed black swans couldn't exist until they reached Australia.

answers.name: Brolga
answers.fact: Famous for elaborate courtship dances.

answers.name: Green tree frog
answers.fact: Notorious for turning up in toilets and downpipes.

answers.name: Barramundi
answers.fact: Most start life male and become female as they grow.

answers.name: Australian brush-turkey
answers.fact: Males build huge compost mounds to incubate the eggs.

answers.name: Australian pelican
answers.fact: Has the longest bill of any bird.

answers.name: Wedge-tailed eagle
answers.fact: Australia's largest bird of prey.

answers.name: Tawny frogmouth
answers.fact: Usually mistaken for an owl, but closer to nightjars.

answers.name: Tree kangaroo
answers.fact: Kangaroos that live in trees, in far north Queensland's rainforests.

answers.name: Bettong
answers.fact: Little 'rat-kangaroos' that dig up underground fungi.

answers.name: Potoroo
answers.fact: A rabbit-sized relative of the kangaroo.

answers.name: Greater glider
answers.fact: Glides up to 100 metres and lives almost entirely on gum leaves.

answers.name: Feathertail glider
answers.fact: The smallest gliding mammal in the world, about mouse-sized.

answers.name: Antechinus
answers.fact: Males die after one frantic breeding season.

answers.name: Dunnart
answers.fact: Mouse-sized, but a carnivorous marsupial.

answers.name: Pygmy possum
answers.fact: The mountain pygmy possum hibernates under the snow.

answers.name: Cuscus
answers.fact: A slow, possum-like animal from Cape York's rainforests.

answers.name: Thorny devil
answers.fact: Drinks by channelling dew through grooves in its skin to its mouth.

answers.name: Shingleback
answers.fact: Pairs often reunite with the same partner year after year.

answers.name: Perentie
answers.fact: Australia's biggest lizard, growing to about 2.5 metres.

answers.name: Corroboree frog
answers.fact: Striking yellow and black, and critically endangered.

answers.name: Queensland lungfish
answers.fact: A 'living fossil'. One in a Chicago aquarium lived past 90.

answers.name: Murray cod
answers.fact: Australia's largest freshwater fish.

answers.name: Yabby
answers.fact: A freshwater crayfish, traditionally caught with string and a bit of meat.

answers.name: Superb fairywren
answers.fact: Mothers teach their unhatched chicks a 'password' call.

answers.name: Willie wagtail
answers.fact: Small, but bold enough to harass eagles.

answers.name: Noisy miner
answers.fact: A native honeyeater, often confused with the introduced Indian myna.

answers.name: Butcherbird
answers.fact: Stores its prey by wedging it onto thorns or into forks of branches.

answers.name: Gang-gang cockatoo
answers.fact: The ACT's bird emblem. Its call sounds like a creaky door.

answers.name: Major Mitchell's cockatoo
answers.fact: One called Cookie lived to 83 at a Chicago zoo.

answers.name: Bush stone-curlew
answers.fact: Its eerie night-time wail gets mistaken for screaming.

answers.name: Malleefowl
answers.fact: Spends months adjusting its egg mound to keep it at the right temperature.

answers.name: Southern boobook
answers.fact: Named after its 'boo-book' call.

answers.name: Peacock spider
answers.fact: Males dance and flash a rainbow flap to impress females.

answers.name: Bogong moth
answers.fact: Migrates around 1,000 km to alpine caves, steering partly by the stars.

answers.name: Bull ant
answers.fact: Among the most aggressive ants in the world.

answers.name: Honeypot ant
answers.fact: Some workers swell with nectar to act as living storage jars.

answers.name: Witchetty grub
answers.fact: A traditional bush food said to taste a bit like almond when cooked.

answers.name: Christmas beetle
answers.fact: Named because it turns up in big numbers around December.

answers.name: Jabiru
answers.fact: Australia's only stork.

answers.name: Gastric-brooding frog
answers.fact: Swallowed its eggs and gave birth through its mouth. Extinct since the 1980s.

answers.name: Night parrot
answers.fact: So elusive it was feared extinct until it was photographed in 2013.

answers.name: Kowari
answers.fact: A small carnivorous marsupial of the stony gibber deserts.

answers.name: Mulgara
answers.fact: A desert marsupial that can get all its water from its food.

answers.name: Plains-wanderer
answers.fact: A ground bird with no close living relatives.

answers.name: Ningaui
answers.fact: A marsupial weighing just a few grams that hunts insects nearly its own size.

answers.name: Numbat
answers.fact: Western Australia's emblem. It eats up to 20,000 termites a day.
